extracted.intended_audience: campus ministry publicity coordinators / volunteers preparing press releases and PSAs for InterVarsity large group events
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for formatting, content, and timing when preparing press releases and short public service announcements (PSAs) for campus ministry large-group events and media distribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Set margins at 15 and 70
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original wording provided; likely intended page margin/column settings for print/layout. Follow the specified margin measurements when preparing the document for media.

rubrics_metrics.name: Double space the release
rubrics_metrics.description: Double space (to allow for their editing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use double spacing throughout so editors can mark changes and make notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include identifying info in upper-left corner
rubrics_metrics.description: Place in upper left hand corner: – one word description of article – your name and phone number – date submitted – number of lines in article
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Put these items together in the upper-left so editors can quickly identify the story, contact person, submission date, and length (lines) for print planning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heading: For Immediate Release
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicate that the material is available to the media immediately; use this exact heading.

rubrics_metrics.name: Start the article mid-page
rubrics_metrics.description: Begin the article almost half-way down the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place the story copy so there is space above (traditional press-release formatting), which helps editors see the header and contact info and mimics a release sheet layout.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mark continuing pages with MORE
rubrics_metrics.description: Write “MORE” at the bottom of each page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a release continues to another page, put "MORE" at the bottom so editors know the story continues.

rubrics_metrics.name: End the article with ****
rubrics_metrics.description: At the end of the article type: * * * *
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the traditional asterisk block to signal the end of the release copy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flag most important parts
rubrics_metrics.description: Mark those parts of the article that are most important so that they don’t get edited out.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and emphasize key facts/sentences (e.g., lead facts, sponsor, date/time/location, contact) to ensure they survive editorial cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Length: several paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: The press release should be several paragraphs in length.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide sufficient detail and structure (lead, supporting paragraphs, boilerplate/contact) rather than a single-sentence notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The first paragraph should include the name of the sponsoring group, name of program (speaker), brief descriptive phrases, date, day, time and place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the lead contains the essential who/what/when/where and a short descriptive hook so editors can quickly grasp the event.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final paragraph contact and ticket details
rubrics_metrics.description: The last paragraph should include details on who to contact for more information and ticket information (if appropriate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full contact info (name, phone/email) and any ticketing or registration instructions so reporters and readers know how to follow up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Send releases by mail at least 10 days in advance
rubrics_metrics.description: Send the press release by mail at least 10 days in advance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow lead time for editorial calendars; include extra materials (see guidance) and follow up with a phone call to confirm receipt and details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include photos and background material when available
rubrics_metrics.description: Include glossy photos and extra background material if available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide media-ready visuals and supplemental info to increase pickup chances; package materials professionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Call to confirm release information
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow up distribution with a phone call to the media contact to ensure they received the release and to answer questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA: treat like short press release
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat this like a short press release to be given verbally for radio or TV.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compose PSAs with the same essential facts as a release but written for spoken delivery—concise and clear.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA: indicate seconds instead of lines
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate the number of seconds (instead of lines) for the Public Service Announcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Estimate and label the running time in seconds so broadcasters can schedule the spot accurately.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA: one-paragraph content
rubrics_metrics.description: A Public Service Announcement should be no more than one paragraph consisting of the information in the first and last paragraphs of a Press Release.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compress the lead and contact/ticket information into a single concise paragraph suitable for on-air reading.

rubrics_metrics.name: PSA timing: send 10 days in advance and confirm
rubrics_metrics.description: Send out the Public Service Announcement 10 days in advance; call to confirm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As with press releases, provide lead time and follow up by phone to increase the chance of broadcast.
